quote: The Queen began the morning in the small domestic orbit she had kept for herself at Windsor: a single room of pale curtains, a brass kettle, a row of shoes lined as if for inspection.
They walked out together with no fanfare.
"It is odd," she said, looking straight ahead, "how public everything feels even when one is alone."
She opened the journal, though she did not write long. The day had already changed shape: the walk had cost her nothing public but it had also given her, quietly, an altered view of the day to come.
"When the tray arrived the Queen lifted the cloth a little and smiled as if alone in a room that had always been hers.",
"There was no triumph in it—only relief."
"The lady-in-waiting offered her support and discretion, as she had at the walk."
The Queen resumed her walk, the actress returned to her view of stone and shadow, and the small choreography of the day closed without a larger step.
She gave the kind of look that settled matters—the brief, impervious fold of a mouth that said she would take the measure herself.
The Queen spoke at last, not of what had happened—the glance was, after all, an event too small to need announcing—but of the tea that would be waiting and the hour’s length.
On the narrow writing table, half in shadow, lay a book closed like a promise.
There was no lightness in the face, only a measurement of the room and of the woman she had learned to trust.
She had been at it for ten minutes when the lady entered: the soft, known tread of someone made for houses that are polite and implacable in equal measure.
